lines.say: Harvard found CEOs lose half their customers every five years.
That came from a Bain fellow, in 1996.
Start with a hundred customers. Five years later, fifty are gone.
And here's the fucked up part. They never storm out, they just stop showing up.
No call, no complaint, and no goodbye.
His point: the longer customers stay, the more they're worth.
And new customers cost money to find. Old ones already know you.
Finding a new client takes ads and luck. Keeping an old one can take a text.
Look at your own books. Which regulars haven't you seen in two months?
Message Health finds those clients and texts them before they become part of the half you lost.
Comment KEEP to get a full retention audit.
